cited_evidence: Behavioural criteria require selecting all qualifying or fallback demand records and retaining only allowed record identities without silently omitting stipulated records.
Top-level corpus includes record_id n06-r01 with demand_score 9, need 'isolate faulty execution branches before replay', source_id s01, source_weight 5.
Job 1 output needs and evidence_sources start at n06-r02 and contain seven records, omitting n06-r01; metadata record_count and evidence_source_count are both 7.
select_demand source selects corpus rows with demand_score >= 3 or fallback IDs n06-r07/n06-r08, so n06-r01 qualifies under the visible selection rule.
normalize source defines allowed_record_ids as ['n06-r09','n06-r02','n06-r03','n06-r04','n06-r05','n06-r06','n06-r07','n06-r08'], excluding n06-r01, then filters normalized_df by that list.
initial_receipt.explanation: The two-job execution is faulty because the stipulated corpus contains eight qualifying demand records: all records n06-r01 through n06-r08 have demand_score >= 3. Job 1 output contains only seven records and omits n06-r01, which should have been selected and handed downstream. The supplied function evidence localizes the omission to normalize, whose allowed_record_ids excludes n06-r01 and therefore filters it out after selection.
